text:
marta: Heads-up — starting int4 quant-sweep for Nucleus14B (hybrid Llama+Mistral head layout). Short prompts look fine, but with 8k summaries I'm seeing token drift + repeated chunks after ~2k tokens. Anyone seen kv-cache offsets with mixed head layouts?

simon: can you paste the exact command and a failing example?

marta: sure — repro command I'm running locally:

```
./bench_infer --model=nucleus14b --quant=int4 --seq_len=8192 --batch=1 --prompt-file=tests/long_summaries.txt --use-kvcache --cache-mode=streaming
```

marta: example diff (model vs hf-baseline):
- HF: "In summary, the patient ... stable."
- Nucleus14B int4: "In summary, the patient ... stable. In summary, the patient ..." (repeats after token ~2048)

jia: did you run the tokenizer conversion step? Nucleus uses a merged vocab + alternate BOS/EOS ids in the bridge script, those can cause off-by-n mappings if mapping table is stale.

marta: used hf-convert.py from repo/tools and passed `--merge-unk true`. Ran a quick token-id check: looks fine for first 100 tokens.

nate: can you run the mapping checker? e.g.

```
python tools/check_vocab_mapping.py --src hf --dst redwood --sample "The patient was"
```

nate: that will print any token id offsets >0 across the vocab slice.

marta: ran it — shows a consistent +2 offset for token ids >50265 (end of vocab block). Not sure why only high ids.

simon: hmm. Another angle: quant packing order (QPack v1 vs v2) can reorder per-head kernel memory layout. If pack expects per-layer layout but weights are per-head, kv pointers will be wrong once the cache wraps.

deploy-bot: deployment nucleus14b-int4 passed smoke tests — latency median 120ms, p95 310ms :white_check_mark: but quality eval failed (ROUGE Δ -0.18 vs baseline).

jia: also try toggling the positional embedding handling. Nucleus uses hybrid rotary where some heads use per-head phase scale. If runtime picks "per-layer" mode it will misapply sin/cos and cause phase drift long-term. Try env toggle: `REDWOOD_ROPE_MODE=perhead` vs `legacy`.

marta: switched to REDWOOD_ROPE_MODE=perhead and reran. Alignment is correct up to ~2048 tokens, but repeats still appear after kv-wrap.

nate: can you patch in the kv_cache_stride_fix from origin/kv-fix-2026 branch? That one corrects wrap index calculation when head_stride != kv_stride. Also try rebuild with QPack v2 which preserves head-order.

marta: starting a rebuild with qpack=v2 + kv-fix patch now. Will run the long-sweep overnight. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

simon: small diagnostic to run in meantime — dump kv indices around wrap: add `--dump-kv-idx=2040-2060` to bench and attach logs. If we see sudden jump it's arithmetic mismatch.

marta: good call. attaching snippet in a bit.

jia: one more: ensure tokenizer normalization path uses NFKC — I've seen multi-byte diacritics cause different codepoint sequences which then trigger different rotatory phase groups when tokenized mid-sequence. Run `tools/token_norm_check.py --mode=nfkc` against sample.

marta: will add that to the sweep.

simon: thanks — if kv-fix+qpack v2 clears the regression we should plan a lightweight canary rollout on dedicated infra before hosted. Also add an eval set that exercises >4k contexts so we don't regress again.

marta: TL;DR next steps: 1) rebuild with qpack=v2 + kv-fix branch, 2) run `--dump-kv-idx` around wrap points, 3) run tokenizer nfkc check, 4) overnight int4 sweep and longctx ROUGE eval. Will post results tomorrow. :thumbsup:

marta: pinging @simon @jia @nate if anything else to add.
